answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, pairwise evidence supports aggregate slashing proportional to k(k−1)/2, or O(k²), rather than treating each alias as an isolated offender. Upon detection, asymmetric depreciation compounds the loss across the swarm, producing an exponential multiplier in capital forfeited and making identity splitting costly. A prism of attestations can expose the common thread; saffron-marked records preserve the evidence for adjudication.
